title: Resource forecasting playbook — heterogeneous GPU pool
summary: Working playbook used by Solutions Engineering during early customer POCs when recommending a dedicated, heterogeneous GPU pool. Focus is on realistic forecasting, autoscale guardrails, and simple cost sensitivity knobs that non-infra customers can understand. This is intentionally pragmatic — not a full R&D doc — and meant to be used in workshops and customer proposals.
workshop_objectives: (1) Build a 3-scenario forecast (baseline / steady growth / peak-oriented) tied to measurable customer SLAs; (2) produce simple autoscale rules and prewarm recommendations; (3) quantify hourly cost delta for 3 GPU mixes; (4) capture operational risks and fallbacks for each scenario.
audience_and_prereqs: Customer infra owners, platform engineers, and product/ML leads. Prereqs: sample qps distribution for payloads (p95 tokens per request), expected concurrency, preferred latency SLO, and desired cost band (target $/1000 requests). If data missing, use defaults in assumptions below.
sizing_assumptions:
Defaults used in the workshop if customer numbers are unavailable:
- Avg request: 350 tokens generated, median prompt 50 tokens
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 500ms for interactive chat, p95 <= 1.2s for standard generation
- Model choices: smaller-variant (13B int8 optimized) and larger-variant (70B q4f16-like)
- GPU types: A10G (cost‑efficient), A100-40GB (balanced), H100-80GB (high throughput)
- KV-cache warm hit ratio target: 40% steady-state after 24h of traffic during normal hours
- Batching behavior: continuous batching with max batch window 12ms for interactive tier
- Node overhead: ~10% GPU time for orchestration and other guests in multi-tenant pools
- Prewarm latency buffer: 10% of peak pool for instant capacity (prewarmed replicas)
three_scenarios: Scenario A — Baseline (early production): 25 qps sustained daytime, 75 qps peak bursts for short periods. Estimated concurrency: 50 active requests. Recommended pool: mixed A10G (4), A100 (1) with 1 prewarm on A100. Scenario B — Growth (scale to business metrics): 100 qps sustained, 300 qps peaks. Estimated concurrency: 200. Recommended pool: A10G (12), A100 (4), 1 H100 reserved for heavy large-model ops plus 4 prewarm A10G replicas. Scenario C — Enterprise SLA (predictable throughput): 400 qps sustained, 900 qps peaks with guaranteed headroom. Estimated concurrency: 800. Recommended pool: H100 (6), A100 (8), A10G (12), with autoscale headroom to add 30% burst capacity and 20 prewarm replicas across tiers.
autoscale_policy_recommendation:
Principles: prefer fast vertical scaling via adding more replicas of cost‑efficient GPUs for common small-model paths, reserve 1–2 larger GPUs for heavy requests, and enforce hard throttles when cost budget exceeded. Concrete rule set:
- Metric: cpu/gpu-utilization smoothed 20s window + request queue depth
- Scale-up triggers: sustained GPU util > 70% for 30s OR queue depth > 5 for 15s
- Scale-down triggers: GPU util < 30% for 120s and no queued requests
- Prewarm policy: maintain N prewarmed replicas (N = ceil(avg_peak_qps * prewarm_fraction / single_replica_throughput)). Default prewarm_fraction = 0.15 for interactive apps.
- Fallback policy: if autoscale cannot provision within time threshold (e.g., cloud provisioning > 60s), route new requests to a cheaper hosted instance with degraded SLO and add to log/alerting channel.
- Cost guardrail: weekly cost burn-rate cap that will trigger automated throttling of non-critical routes and notify customer success.
heterogeneous_pool_guidance: Mixing GPU classes reduces unit cost while preserving burst capacity. Practical tips: dedicate H100s to large-model, long-context inference and KV-heavy chains; use A10G/A100 for smaller models and high qps; colocate similar-memory-models on the same instance class to reduce fragmentation. Reserve 10–20% GPU memory headroom per host to avoid OOM from sudden token spikes.
cost_estimates_table:
Rough cloud list/operational costs (USD/hr) used for quick customer math during workshops:
- A10G equivalent: $1.25/hr
- A100-40GB: $3.60/hr
- H100-80GB: $9.50/hr
Notes: include ~20% on top for ancillary infra (storage, networking, control-plane) and another 10% for reserved capacity premiums in enterprise contracts. Examples:
- Scenario A cost band (on-demand): A10G x4 + A100 x1 -> 4*1.25 + 3.6 = $8.6/hr -> add 30% margin = $11.18/hr
- Scenario B baseline: 12*A10G + 4*A100 + 1*H100 -> 12*1.25 + 4*3.6 + 9.5 = 15 + 14.4 + 9.5 = $38.9/hr -> +30% ops margin = $50.57/hr
- Scenario C reserved blend: 12*A10G + 8*A100 + 6*H100 -> 15 + 28.8 + 57 = $100.8/hr -> with reserved discounts and commitments expect 30–45% lower effective hourly cost depending on contract.
operational_risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: cold-start tail latency during sudden traffic spikes. Mitigation: aggressive prewarm for interactive routes and a fast fallback to hosted variant.
- Risk: inefficient packing across GPU types leading to overprovisioning. Mitigation: scheduling affinity by model size and memory class; regular weekly packing sweep jobs.
- Risk: unexpected model regressions cause repeated re-runs and cost blowouts. Mitigation: tie rollout cadence to canary traffic with token/cost limits and automated rollback thresholds.
- Risk: quota/provisioning delays from cloud provider when scaling H100s. Mitigation: keep small hot pool of reserved H100s for critical fallbacks and use cheaper classes for scale-out.
customer_worksheet_template: (copy into spreadsheet) Input: target p95 latency (ms) | avg generated tokens | target qps profile (min/avg/peak) | preferred models list | cost target $/1000 requests. Output: recommended pool mix, prewarm count, autoscale thresholds, expected hourly and monthly cost estimate. Use scenario toggles for committed discount levels (0/25/40%).
next_steps_for_se: 1) Run quick pool-sim with customer-provided qps trace (use repo link in linked artifacts). 2) Prepare slide one-pager with recommended pool and cost bands. 3) If customer is comfortable, propose a 30-day POC with a small reserved commitment (e.g., 1–2 A100 equivalents) to validate tail behavior. 4) Capture iteration-specific telemetry keys to track (p95 latency by route, token burn per route, prewarm hit ratio).
